personality_one_liner: A highly accessible, tactile, and friendly local companion that makes booking rides and market runs in Tagkawayan feel effortless, safe, and community-driven.

spacing.rule: Generous padding everywhere to prevent mis-taps. Minimum 56pt height for list items and buttons. Use xl (24pt) between major sections.

do's: Use on the bottom tab bar and bottom-sheet headers to follow native iOS patterns.
Ensure a translucent tinted base (>=70% opacity) beneath foreground text over glass.
For low-end Android (common in rural areas), fallback to solid surfaceSecondary to maintain performance.
dont's: Do not use on generic list rows, form inputs, or standard cards.
Avoid heavy blur overlays on map interfaces that might cause rendering stutters on low-end devices.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: Provide immediate, high-contrast access to the two core services: Book a Ride and Pabili Market.

states.loading: A friendly skeleton loader for the main cards and recent activity.
states.empty: No recent activity yet. 'Ready for your first ride or market run?' with an illustration.
states.error: Failed to load recent activity. Friendly 'Oops, connection hiccup' with a retry button.

screens.layout: Header with user greeting and current local weather/time (to feel localized). Two massive, chunky touch cards stacked vertically or side-by-side (if width allows). Card 1 (Book a Ride): brandPrimary tinted background with the tricycle image and gradient scrim. Card 2 (Pabili): brandSecondary tinted background with market produce image and gradient scrim. Below them: 'Recent Activity' list.

screens.name: Book a Ride
screens.purpose: Allow users to set pickup and dropoff within Tagkawayan and see the COD fare estimate.

states.loading: Skeleton placeholders for address fields and map initialization.
states.error: Unable to calculate route. 'Can't reach the map service right now.' + Retry.

screens.layout: Full-screen map view in background. Bottom sheet covering the bottom 40% with stacked, chunky inputs for 'Pickup' and 'Dropoff'. Floating action button (FAB) for 'My Location'. Primary sticky CTA 'Find a Driver' securely anchored at the bottom with safe area padding. Uses a 500-weight typography for legibility.

screens.name: Pabili Store Browse
screens.purpose: Let users type a custom shopping list or select preset local store items.

states.empty: No stores open? 'Stores are sleeping. Try a custom list!'
states.error: Failed to load catalog. Retry button.

screens.layout: Tabs at the top: 'Browse Preset' | 'Type Custom List'. Browse tab: A 2-column grid (flexWrap: wrap, space-between) of tactile categories (Produce, Meat, Groceries). Custom list tab: A large, comfortable text area (surfaceTertiary background) filling the screen, asking 'What do you need?'. Sticky CTA 'Request Pabili' fixed to the bottom of the screen above keyboard.

screens.name: Order Tracking
screens.purpose: Show live status of the ride or delivery with driver details.
screens.layout: Large status typography at the top ('Driver is on the way!'). A pulsing progress indicator. A chunky tactile card in the center showing driver details (Avatar fallback initials in brandPrimary circle, name, tricycle number). Sticky CTA 'Call Driver' at the bottom.

screens.name: Driver Dashboard
screens.purpose: Dedicated interface for drivers to accept rides and update status.

states.empty: Illustration of a parked tricycle with 'You're online! Waiting for requests in Tagkawayan.'

screens.layout: Use surfaceInverse for the header area to clearly distinguish Driver Mode from Customer Mode. A massive, tactile 'Go Online / Offline' toggle. The main feed is a list of incoming request cards (pickup, dropoff, fare) with large, friendly 'Accept' (brandPrimary) and 'Decline' (surfaceTertiary) buttons.

hero_market.alt: Fresh organic produce at a local market

instructions_to_main_agent: CRITICAL: Zero tolerance for font weights above 500. Use typography sizing (xl, 2xl) to convey hierarchy, not bold/black font weights.
CRITICAL: Absolutely NO blue/indigo/purple colors in this app. Use the defined 'info' token (slate grey) for any informational banners.
Ensure all primary actions (e.g., 'Find a Driver', 'Request Pabili') are anchored as Sticky CTAs at the bottom of the screen, outside scrolling regions, with proper safe-area padding.
When placing text over the 'hero_tricycle' or 'hero_market' images, a gradient scrim (top-to-bottom, transparent to >=70% surfaceInverse) is MANDATORY to guarantee legibility.
The app targets non-technical users. Rely heavily on large touch targets (minimum 56pt) and tactile (shadow tier 2) chunky cards. Avoid subtle hidden gestures or swipe-to-delete patterns.
Driver Mode should instantly look different from Customer Mode. Use the surfaceInverse token aggressively in the driver header so they know they are in 'work' mode.
Web Search learnings applied: Avoid dense 'super app' 12-icon walls (like full Gojek). Tagkawayan only needs two massive entry points for Ride and Pabili to maintain simplicity and approachability.
